subject: Renewal: Dedicated pool increase & SLA addendum
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <olivia@helix.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@helix.ai>
Date: 2027-04-21T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: dedicated capacity renewal

Marcus —

We're coming up on our Dedicated pool renewal for Q2. The team has a new set of requirements: we need to increase reserved GPUs from 16 to 24 (NVIDIA H100-equivalent), and guarantee a sustained throughput target for our prod inference jobs (targeting ~120k tokens/min sustained; peak bursts higher).

Before we start the PO, two asks: 1) can Redwood provide a clear SLA addendum covering throughput and P95 latency targets for the larger pool? 2) if we push latency/uptime targets tighter, what is the credit structure you offer for exceptions (we've had a couple of burst-related P95 spikes this quarter and want to understand remedies)?

Budget is approved internally but procurement needs pricing + the SLA language to finalize. Attached is a short outline of our throughput profile.

Thanks —
Olivia Grant
Head of Platform
Helix.ai

Attachment: helix_proposal_v1.pdf (summary of throughput requirements)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@helix.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-22T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: dedicated capacity renewal

Olivia —

Thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the profile. We can definitely support a reservation increase to 24 H100-equivalent GPUs and work up throughput guarantees. High level: we propose 24-GPU reserved pool with an SLA addendum that commits to 99.80% uptime for the pool and a P95 generation latency target of 200ms for baseline traffic (your described sustained throughput). For scheduled heavy-burst windows (training/large-batch inference), we recommend defining windows where a relaxed P95 (up to 350ms) applies; in those windows we can offer a credit mechanism rather than the standard latency rebate.

I'll attach a draft commercial proposal and a first-pass SLA addendum. For the SLA exception (i.e., relaxing the P95 during planned bursts) we typically document the windows and add a proportional credit table (example: a 10% monthly usage credit if latency exceedance is due to capacity oversubscription during declared burst windows). If you want tighter latency outside burst windows, we'll need a commensurate reserved top-up or burst buffer.

Next steps: 1) confirm the 24-GPU spec and target throughput windows; 2) I'll loop in finance and legal for the explicit credit language; 3) if acceptable I'll send a DocuSign-ready addendum.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: helix_proposal_v1.pdf (pricing sheet)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-23T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: dedicated capacity renewal — Helix.ai (internal approvals)

Team — looping you in. Helix wants to go from 16 -> 24 reserved GPUs and wants explicit P95 + throughput commitments. Initial proposal attached with our suggested credit structure for burst windows. Key points:
- Estimated uplift ARR: +$145k annually (paper).
- Proposed uptime SLA: 99.80%.
- Proposed latency SLO: 200ms P95 for sustained traffic; 350ms P95 allowed during declared burst windows with a 10% usage credit if breached.

Ben — need final pricing approval and confirmation on the credit calculation. Laura — legal to sign off on addendum wording in redlines_terms.docx (attached). Stephanie — can you coordinate with Solutions Eng to validate the throughput numbers and whether a dedicated burst buffer (additional ephemeral capacity) is needed?

Thanks —
Marcus

Attachment: redlines_terms.docx (proposed SLA language with redlines)

Marcus —

Thanks for the fast follow. A couple of clarifications from procurement and engineering:
1) We need the SLA addendum to explicitly call out the measurement windows for P95 and how the burst windows are declared (automated via API or scheduled). Can Redwood support programmatic window declarations (we prefer an API to declare planned bursts at least 48 hours in advance)?
2) The credit table needs to be explicit: what % credit applies for SLA misses at different severity bands and how credits are calculated against monthly reserved fees.
3) Term: Helix prefers a 12-month term for the new reservation, effective on the PO date.

If you can send a DocuSign-ready addendum and the final pricing, procurement will process the PO. I've attached our PO stub.

Regards,
Rajiv
VP Engineering, Helix.ai

Attachment: helix_purchase_order.pdf (PO stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@helix.ai>, Olivia Grant <olivia@helix.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, procurement@helix.ai
Date: 2027-05-03T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal: dedicated capacity renewal

Rajiv / Olivia —

Appreciate the clarifications. We've signed off internally and can accommodate the 24-GPU reserved pool with the following commercial terms (DocuSign link below + SLA addendum attached):

- Term: 12 months from PO execution.
- Capacity: 24 H100-equivalent GPUs reserved for Helix.ai.
- Uptime: 99.80% monthly for the reserved pool.
- Latency (P95): 200ms for baseline sustained workload (measured over 5-minute rolling windows).
- Burst windows: Helix may declare planned burst windows via API or email at least 48 hours in advance. During declared windows, the P95 target is relaxed to 350ms.
- SLA credits: if the P95 target is missed outside declared burst windows, credits scale as follows: Severity 1 (P95 > 350ms outside bursts): 25% monthly reserved-fee credit; Severity 2 (200ms < P95 <= 350ms outside bursts): 10% credit. If misses occur during declared burst windows, we will apply a single-tier credit of 10% monthly reserved-fee if the relaxed P95 (350ms) is exceeded for more than 6 hours cumulative in a billing month.

Notes: 1) credits are applied against the monthly reserved fee only (not variable usage); 2) we will instrument API hooks for Helix to declare windows and for mutual visibility into measured P95; 3) Solutions Eng and your SRE should validate the throughput with a short performance run prior to the contract start date (we can schedule next week).

I've attached the SLA addendum and pushed a DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/helix-rdw-sla. Once signed, finance will issue an invoice and we can align the PO.

Please confirm and I'll mark this as ready-to-sign.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: sla_addendum_helix.pdf (finalized SLA addendum)
